These are the Subverse Rules and VMUN committee Rules of Procedure.

**Subverse Rules**

1. Discussion that is not directly pertinent to VMUN, must be posted in the general discussion thread.

2. Users that have not yet registered in the delegation registration thread and received approval may only post in the general discussion thread.

3. If a committee is marked [Active], only delegates registered for that committee may post top-level comments.

*Effective 14 February 2016*

**Rules of Procedure of VMUN for Two-Week Debates**

**MAIN SUBMISSION** Delegates interested in submitting a resolution for debate should make a discussion post containing the resolution. A VMUN officer will then create a new thread and save the resolution. [Learn more about resolution-writing here.](http://www.unausa.org/global-classrooms-model-un/how-to-participate/model-un-preparation/resolutions)

**DURATION** Each standard debate will last a period of two weeks. In the debate period, delegates are expected to check the thread at least once every 12 hours. Each action in the debate will take up to twelve hours, meaning that at least 28 actions will be taken in each debate.

**MAIN SUBMITTER'S STARTING SPEECH** Each resolution will be posted on the listed debate starting time, along with the speech of the main submitter. Delegates will have 12 hours to read the resolution and to raise no more than one point of information (question). In the next 12 hours, the main submitter will answer all of the questions. (Failure to answer all questions, excluding clearly frivolous questions, may affect your future participation in VMUN.)

**POINTS AND MOTIONS** At any point in time, any delegate may raise, in a top-level comment, these points and motions: point of information (question to a speaker who has just concluded their speech), point of parliamentary inquiry (question on VMUN procedure), point of order (if the chair or a delegate is doing something that is not permitted), motion to appeal the decision of the chair. Please note that the following points and motions, and all others not listed above, will not be entertained: motion to divide the house, motion to suspend the meeting, motion to close the debate, motion to extend debate time, point of personal privilege (PM a moderator instead).

**SPEAKING** When the chair asks for speakers, interested delegates should respond. The chair will then reply saying which speaker they will recognize. The speaker is then expected to prepare a speech and post it within the first six hours of the posted time. Then, other delegates will have the rest of the twelve hours to make points of information. After that, twelve hours will be allocated for the speaker to respond to *all* of the points of information
